attempts.summary: I couldn't create `summaries/001266-park-2025-01.md`. The paragraph is below, ready to save: Most of the paper's main findings could not be confirmed here, and many could not be tested. The dandiset holds only example recordings, so the pooled statistics, drug effects and temperature results (29 of 55 claims) are out of reach. Dendritic spikes in the Fig. 2 neuron and the failure, success, success, failure pattern under steps reproduced, though most spikes ride on a third somatic spike. The amplification maps, length constant, two-motif claim, 15 ms rule and plateau duration did not reproduce, most likely because the paper sets thresholds and the distal region by hand without stating them. The published model code does not run as shipped.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Park, Wong-Campos et al. (2025) on dandiset 001266, which holds the example recordings of the paper's figures (raw voltage imaging movies of CA1 pyramidal neurons in slices with their stimulus and patch clamp channels). It counts bAPs and dSpikes in the neuron of Figs. 2 and 3, the step, wide-field and drug examples, measures the plateau examples, and checks the optical recording against patch clamp. A second notebook runs the paper's published NEURON model for its model claims. The pooled samples behind most of the paper's statistics are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.notes: All 83 rows of the Source Data index name a file in the dandiset; they hold 81 distinct names, the 81 subject folders (two files are listed for two panels each). The experiment label in every file opened matches the index's Experiment column. Counts identify the Fig. 3 files: the legend's D2 (49 + 35 = 84 bAPs) is the file named D4 (84 bAPs with the claims file's settings, 85 to 88 with 4 s.d.); the file named D2 has 105 to 110. The Fig. 2 entry (file D3, the legend's "D1 stim") gives the legend's 8 dSpikes. The soma and D4+soma files have 139 to 167 bAPs against the legend's 167 and 170. The Fig. S8 legends' counts (92 and 96 bAPs) do not single out a file: D1 and D2 have 105 to 113. Three recordings are deposited twice.
deviations: Names are matched after the index's spelling (underscores, spaces, stray quotes) is put into DANDI's (hyphens).

outcomes.notes: 8 of 54 trials carry a dSpike under both filter readings, with the claims file's 5 s.d. threshold and with 4 s.d., distal region beyond 300 µm; no dSpike follows the first somatic spike of a trial. The statement says more than the criterion tests, and that part does not hold: 7 to 10 trials have three somatic spikes, not two, and 5 to 7 of the 8 dSpikes ride on the third spike; each dSpike is on the last spike of its trial. With the region cut at 400 µm the Butterworth reading gives 6.
deviations: The distal region is the traced line beyond 300 µm (claims file). The line was traced on the mean image as the brightest ridge, where the paper drew it by hand on a structural image; beyond about 400 µm it runs off the trunk (the mean image along it falls to 0.73 to 0.89 of the image median in the Fig. 2 and 3 files, notebook section "Where the regions lie"), so 300 to 400 µm is shown as a variant.

dSpike threshold at the first minimum of a Gaussian kernel density (Scott bandwidth) of the distal amplitudes above its failure mode (the lowest density peak at least a quarter as high as the highest), with interpolated FWHM < 5 ms. Any minimum above the failure mode counts, whatever the size of the bump beyond it, so a few outlying large amplitudes also get a threshold (the notebook shows how many amplitudes lie above each trough); where the density has no minimum above the failure mode no threshold exists and the dSpike count is undefined, not zero. An assumption: the paper set its thresholds by hand. The claims file places it at the histogram's trough; the trough between the two highest modes (tried while preparing, not in the notebook) falls between two small clusters of dSpikes and was not used.
File D3, the index's Fig. 2 entry (the legend calls the stimulus D1).

outcomes.notes: The two readings the criterion names disagree, so the criterion makes the claim methods_underspecified. A two-component Gaussian mixture is preferred for the distal amplitudes (BIC lower by 55 to 125) and not at the soma (BIC higher by 11 to 12), as the claim says. Hartigan's dip test finds no bimodality at either site (distal p 0.63 to 0.99, soma p 0.70 to 0.93); 8 large events among about 115 are too few for it. The question for the paper's authors is which test, if any, supports "clearly bimodal".

outcomes.notes: The criterion's two thresholds are never met together. With dF/F_ref the -dSpike distal value is 0.72 of the soma's beyond 300 µm, not below half; between 300 and 400 µm it is 0.50 to 0.51, but the +dSpike value is then 0.81 to 0.86 of the soma's, below it; beyond 300 µm the +dSpike threshold alone is met (1.01 to 1.06). With raw -dF/F the -dSpike ratio is 0.27 to 0.44 and the +dSpike ratio 0.38 to 0.74. bAPs with a dSpike are larger in the distal region than bAPs without (dF/F_ref 3.3 against 2.1 beyond 300 µm, 2.6 to 2.8 against 1.5 between 300 and 400 µm).
deviations: The distal region is the traced line beyond 300 µm (claims file). dF_ref is the mean -dF from 10 to 20 ms after each spike relative to the trial's pre-stimulus baseline (Fig. 1d legend), averaged over all bAPs of the file for each segment. With bAPs in bursts and a 20 ms stimulus this window holds the stimulus-driven depolarization, which is largest near the stimulated branch; raw -dF/F is shown as a variant. The paper does not say how F_ref was taken for bursts.
The distal value treats the distal segments as one region (mean peak over mean reference); the paper shows maps and gives no number, and the criterion's half and equal are the claims file's readings.

outcomes.notes: No reading gives 255 ± 10 µm. Per-spike fits of dF/F_ref over the traced trunk (to 400 µm) fail or exceed 5000 µm for 23 to 42% of the -dSpike bAPs, and give a mean λ of 1407 to 1488 µm for A exp(-x/λ) and 54 to 58 µm for A exp(-x/λ) + c, for the Fig. 2 file and for all six files. Fits of raw -dF/F give 356 ± 4 µm (Fig. 2 file, 106 to 110 spikes) and 402 to 404 ± 4 µm (all six files, about 600 spikes) without an offset; with an offset they mostly fail. The amplitude profile rises near the stimulated branch before it falls, which an exponential from the soma does not describe. The sample is 106 to 110 -dSpike bAPs in the Fig. 2 file and 590 to 646 in all six, against the paper's 93.
deviations: The fit runs over the traced trunk to 400 µm; beyond it the line leaves the dendrite. The paper does not give the fit range.
Amplitude is the peak -dF/F in the somatic peak frame and the next 3 frames, relative to the trial's pre-stimulus baseline.

outcomes.notes: With the claims file's settings (5 s.d., beyond 300 µm) one distal event in file D4 (20.7 or 21.4 ms after onset) and one (median filter, 170 ms) or two (Butterworth, 126 and 170 ms) in the D4+soma file have no somatic spike within 15 ms before them, so by the criterion some dSpikes lack a preceding somatic spike. Before the D4+soma events the somatic trace stays at 2.0 to 2.4 s.d.; these events fall between stimuli, with distal amplitudes of 0.74 to 1.03% against thresholds of 0.57 to 0.63%. The filter readings differ on whether the baseline's dSpikes can be counted at all. In 5 of 8 readings (all four median-filter readings, and Butterworth at 4 s.d. between 300 and 400 µm) the baseline's distal amplitudes have no density trough, so no dSpike threshold exists and the count is undefined. In the other 3 (Butterworth) the baseline has 6, 2 and 22 dSpikes, and the 100 nM recording has somatic spikes (1, 1 and 8 bAPs) and no dSpike under the baseline's threshold, as the claim says. Somatic bAPs fall from 18 to 62 to 1 to 12 at 100 nM, and the largest distal amplitude from 1.5 to 3.0% to 0.1 to 0.8%; at 500 nM no somatic spike is found. Under its own threshold (0.34%, below the baseline's 0.96%) the 100 nM file has 4 dSpikes in the Butterworth reading at 4 s.d. beyond 300 µm. dSpike threshold at the first minimum of a Gaussian kernel density (Scott bandwidth) of the distal amplitudes above its failure mode (the lowest density peak at least a quarter as high as the highest), with interpolated FWHM < 5 ms. Any minimum above the failure mode counts, whatever the size of the bump beyond it, so a few outlying large amplitudes also get a threshold (the notebook shows how many amplitudes lie above each trough); where the density has no minimum above the failure mode no threshold exists and the dSpike count is undefined, not zero. An assumption: the paper set its thresholds by hand. The claims file places it at the histogram's trough; the trough between the two highest modes (tried while preparing, not in the notebook) falls between two small clusters of dSpikes and was not used.

Up to the end of the cumulative rise (a) the ratio is 2.58 (+30 ms), 1.35 (+100), 3.77 (-100) and 1.06 (-30), above 2 in two timings. To the end of the epoch (b) the single-stimulus areas sum to a negative value at +30 and -100 ms, so the ratio is undefined there (printed as -2.03 and -9.9), and it is 1.59 and 1.28 at +100 and -30 ms. The dendrite-minus-soma -dF/F is positive from 30 to 300 ms in 8 of 9 cells (7 of 9 with the region beyond 200 µm), but the longest persistence after the stimulus ends is 206 ms (5 ms smoothing) or 222 ms (20 ms) with the region anywhere on the trunk, and 170 or 220 ms beyond 200 µm, short of 270 to 330 in every reading. Cell 160204, with a positive mean difference (+1.3 to +2.7%), returns within 2 s.d. at once (0 to 6 ms) in every reading. The measure counts a deviation of either sign as persisting (002658, with a negative mean difference, gets 134 ms with 20 ms smoothing); counting only a positive difference gives 002658 0 ms and leaves the longest persistence unchanged (206, 222, 170 and 220 ms). Sensitivity is 11.7 ± 2.9% per 100 mV at 1 kHz (10.8 ± 3.5% at 2 kHz), within 12 ± 1.2 on average. The noise-equivalent voltage is 3.5 ± 0.5 mV (reading a) and 3.3 ± 0.9 mV (b) at 1 kHz against 1.2 ± 0.5, and 11.4 and 5.2 mV at 2 kHz against 2.5 ± 0.8. At 1 kHz, 6 of 1106 electrical spikes have no optical match and 19 optical spikes have no electrical one; at 2 kHz, 254 of 1159 are missed and 385 added. The two rates together hold 2265 electrical spikes, close to the paper's 2212. Counting an electrical spike only after the membrane repolarized below -30 mV (largest rate 91 Hz, against 333 and 263 Hz with the 3 ms rule) gives 1105 spikes with 5 missed and 19 added at 1 kHz, and 1107 with 189 missed and 372 added at 2 kHz, so the false detections are not an artefact of the electrical count. Two NEV variants were added. Reading (a) in the quietest 1 s window after the first second gives 2.1 ± 0.6 mV at 1 kHz and 3.4 ± 1.1 mV at 2 kHz. With the Methods' maximum-likelihood pixel weighting it gives 1.9 ± 0.6 and 2.5 ± 0.5 mV (in the first second 3.5 ± 0.7 and 7.6 ± 3.8; reading b 3.2 ± 0.9 and 4.3 ± 0.7), so the 2 kHz value falls within 2.5 ± 0.8 and the 1 kHz value stays above 1.2 ± 0.5; the weights lower the sensitivity to 8.1 ± 2.2% at 1 kHz, and 8 spikes are missed and 20 added at 1 kHz (181 and 297 at 2 kHz). The false detections fail the criterion's zero under every reading, so the outcome does not depend on the NEV.

The Methods' maximum-likelihood weighting ("the fluorescence at each pixel was correlated with the whole-field average fluorescence. Pixels that showed stronger correlation to the mean were preferentially weighted", Methods, Extracting fluorescence from movies) is shown as a variant, each pixel weighted by its regression slope on the whole-field mean over its residual variance, both from frame-to-frame differences so that bleaching does not enter (a choice made here; the paper gives no detail).
NEV reading (a) uses the first second, as before; the quietest 1 s window after it (least variance of the membrane potential) is shown as a variant.
Optical spikes use the claims file's 5 s.d. rule on the high-passed trace; the paper set its threshold by hand.
Membrane potential uses the dandiset description's gain of 50 mV/V.

The share depends on how the pixel waveforms are prepared, which the paper does not give. First five components: centred (each pixel's pre-stimulus mean and the across-pixel mean waveform removed) 22 to 30% over 54 trials and 10 to 12% over 11; baseline removed only, uncentred SVD, 39 to 58% and 16 to 24%; raw counts, uncentred SVD, 100.0% in every case, as the first component is the resting image. Only the raw-count reading meets 86.4%, and it measures resting brightness, not the voltage waveforms; the readings give opposite outcomes and the paper gives no basis to choose. The question is for the paper's authors (finding below).

findings.statement: The paper's Supplementary Software 1 does not run as published: run_morphology.py calls FullCA1Model(channel_params, morphology_file), while FullCA1Model requires a third argument, ka_cutoff (run_simulation.py passes 100). Its cheriff.mod carries non-ASCII characters that NEURON 9 rejects. With these fixed, its step simulation at the soma gives success, success, success, success, failure at 500 µm, not the failure, success, success, failures of Fig. 4f. Its phase-diagram sweeps (Plot_Phase_Diagrams.m grids, 429 runs) give the motif in 11, 17 and 0 cells, none at the Table 1 parameters, where the matrices published in the same zip give 51, 48 and 88, including every Table 1 cell. FullCA1Model registers a per-step callback that outlives the model, so runs in one process slow down and can affect each other.

The dandiset holds the example recordings of the figures (the 83 rows of the Source Data index, 84 files), not the pooled samples behind the paper's statistics: the 17 neurons of Fig. 3, the 43 branches of Fig. 4b, the 28 cells of Fig. 5b, the drug series of Figs. 6 and S16 to S18, the temperature series, the patch recordings of Fig. S1 and the calibration series of Figs. S3 to S5. 29 of the 55 claims cannot be tested for this reason.

The files hold only raw camera movies and DAQ channels. They carry no pixel size, no structural (2P or HiLo) or eYFP images, no stimulus masks, and no regions of interest, so distances from the soma, stimulus positions and the user-drawn regions of the paper cannot be recovered from the files. The pixel size used here (0.65 µm) is from the Methods.

Every file is its own subject: subject_id is the file name (81 subjects for 84 files), date_of_birth is 1900-01-01 and sex is U. Animals and cells can be told apart only through the file names (for example PP070-P16-Cell2).

Three recordings are deposited twice with identical sizes and first frames: sub-153924PP070-P27-Cell1-soma-step-5ms (one copy named without a session), sub-000919PP070-P17-V2-11-freq-opto and sub-000820PP070-P17-V2-11-freq-opto-2khz (two copies each, with different obj- suffixes).

Camera frames are 1.03 ms apart (971 Hz; 1.04 ms in one file) where the paper states 1 kHz, and 0.52 ms (1923 Hz) where it states 2 kHz. The movie and the DAQ record span the same time, so the timestamps are consistent; the stated rates are rounded.

The camera series has "no description", and the DAQ channels are named only by short labels that differ between files for the same signal (the EFS trigger is stim1, stim1 (distal), EC, EC_elec or EC_stim). The amplifier gains are given only in the dandiset description, not in the files.

File names and figure legends name stimulus sites differently: the Fig. 2 legend's "D1 stim" is the file named D3, and the Fig. 3 legend's D2 is the file named D4 (its bAP count, 84, matches the legend's 49 + 35). The Source Data index resolves the first; counts resolve the second.

In the Fig. 2 recording 7 to 10 of the 54 trials have three somatic spikes, where the paper says each stimulus evoked two, and most dSpikes ride on the third spike, where the paper says they always emerged from the second.

Question for the paper's authors: what somatic spike threshold, dSpike threshold and distal region (its far end along the dendrite) were used for the bAP and dSpike counts of Figs. 2 to 4 and S8 to S18? The Methods say the thresholds were set by hand and the region was typically beyond 300 µm. Here a somatic threshold of 5 robust s.d. misses spikes in bursts (139 to 150 against the legend's 167 and 170 bAPs), and the counts for Fig. 3f move from 46 to 51 of 54 when the region stops at 400 µm. In several example recordings (the Fig. S15 file beyond 300 µm, the TTX baseline under the median filter, the Ni2+ file of Fig. S18g) the density of the distal amplitudes has no minimum above its failure mode, so no trough threshold exists. In the file of the Fig. 3 legend's D2, the first-bAP count is within tolerance under one high-pass filter and just outside it under the other (32 and 31 of 54, tolerance 31.5 to 38.5).

Question for the paper's authors: how was dF_ref taken when bAPs come in bursts during a 20 ms stimulus, and over what range and with what amplitude measure was the length constant of Fig. 2h fitted? With the reference 10 to 20 ms after each spike (Fig. 1d legend) the normalized profiles rise near the stimulated branch and per-spike exponential fits fail or give 54 or about 1400 µm; raw amplitudes give 356 µm.

Question for the paper's authors: over what window were the AUCs of Figs. 5 and 6 integrated? Up to the end of the cumulative rise, a single bAP with EFS gives ratios above 2 at two timings in the one cell available; to the end of the epoch, the single-stimulus areas are near zero and no ratio exceeds 2.

Question for the paper's authors: how was the noise-equivalent voltage of Fig. S2 defined, and on which pixels (weighted or not)? With the unweighted cell region it is 3.3 to 3.5 mV at 1 kHz here, against 1.2 ± 0.5 mV.

Question for the paper's authors: which pixels and what preprocessing went into the PCA of Fig. S7b? On the stimulus-triggered pixel waveforms of the Fig. 3a recording the first five components hold 22 to 30% of the variance when the waveforms are centred, 39 to 58% when only each pixel's baseline is removed, and 100% on raw counts, where the first component is the resting image.

entries.name: 001266-park-2025
entries.title: Dendritic spikes and back-propagation in CA1 neurons (Park, Wong-Campos et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Park, Wong-Campos et al. (2025) on dandiset 001266, which holds the example recordings of the paper's figures (raw voltage imaging movies of CA1 pyramidal neurons in slices with their stimulus and patch clamp channels). It counts bAPs and dSpikes in the neuron of Figs. 2 and 3, the step, wide-field and drug examples, measures the plateau examples, and checks the optical recording against patch clamp. A second notebook runs the paper's published NEURON model for its model claims. The pooled samples behind most of the paper's statistics are not in the dandiset.
